location: 06_gd_a / 07_gd_b; U603/U606/U703/U706 pin 7 CLMPI on CLMP_S1..S4; D605/D608, D617/D620, D705/D708, D717/D720 (PMEG4010CEJ, K=CLMP_Sx, A=G_Sxa/b); gen/gdrv.py channel() paralleled-gate branch
finding: The paralleled-gate Miller clamp cannot turn on when it is needed. The UCC21710 compares the CLMPI pin itself against VCLMPTH, and only then turns on its clamp FET. Each gate reaches CLMPI through a Schottky (anode at the gate), so CLMPI charges to about VGS(on) during every on-time. After turn-off nothing pulls it down: the net CLMP_Sx has only the two diode cathodes and pin 7. So the clamp is still off when the complementary device hard-turns-on, about 200 ns later. The cell's own analysis says the clamp is mandatory.
evidence: docs/datasheets/gate-drivers/UCC21710.pdf p26 Fig 8-4 + 8.3.6: the VCLMPTH Schmitt comparator input and the clamp NMOS drain are both on the CLMPI node, with no other pull-down. p9: VCLMPTH = VEE+1.5..2.5 V, tDCLMPI 15-50 ns. docs/datasheets/protection/PMEG4010CEJ.pdf p3: IR 1.1 uA typ at 10 V/25 C (nA at -40 C), Cd 69 pF. Leakage discharge of a >=60 pF node by 22 V takes 60p*22/2u = 0.7 ms, against 31 us period and 200 ns dead time. Capacitive coupling depends on the unspecified CLMPI pin capacitance. sim/out/pv_design/report.md sec 4: without the clamp the off gate reaches +2.68 V, above VGS(th) min 1.9 V (docs/datasheets/power-semiconductors/MSC035SMA170B4.pdf p2), at 1100 V/72.4 A. cell_spec gate_drive.miller_clamp says 'required'. Netlist: CLMP_S1 = D605.1 D608.1 U603.7 only.
proposed_fix: Give CLMP_Sx a defined discharge to the off-state level, e.g. 100-470 R from CLMP_Sx to OUTL_Sx in gdrv.channel(). That adds no static current: OUTL sits at gate potential when on. With tau ~ R x ~100 pF the clamp engages about 50-150 ns after turn-off, near the end of the gate fall and inside the 200 ns dead time. Alternatively replace the diodes with ~1-2 R per gate. Re-run the DPT deck with the real network (diode + R + VCLMPTH) and confirm the off gate stays below VGS(th).

location: 03_power; R301/R302 (leg A), R303/R304 (leg B) 4.99R 2512 1 W, C303/C304, C307/C308 2x4.7n 2 kV; gen/pvcell.py calc() 'damp'
finding: The RC damper dissipates 3-7x the power the design check assumes, and more than the 2 x 1 W 2512 resistors are rated for. design_check gives 0.89 W per leg from 2 x 0.5 x 2Coss x Vos^2 x f. That ignores the loop energy and the Qoss commutated through the damper at every hard turn-on. The damper energy barely changes with C, so a smaller C is not a fix. Peak damper current also puts about 240 V across each 4.99 R, above the 200 V element rating stated in the drawing note.
evidence: ngspice 46 runs, scratch decks in review_pvcell/spice. (1) The spec's own deck sim/spice/pv_dpt_MSC035SMA170B4x2_2L_1100V.cir puts 214 uJ per cycle into its 10 R damper = 6.8 W at 32 kHz. (2) The drawn RC (2.35 nF + 9.98 R) at the device pins, with the 20 nH loop as cap ESL 8.5 nH + 11.5 nH, bulk 15 nH away and the same VDMOS model, gives per cycle: 185 uJ at 1100 V/72 A, 157 uJ at 950 V/62 A, 122 uJ at 800 V/45 A, 113 uJ at 950 V/28 A, 87-95 uJ at 550-600 V. That is 2.8-5.9 W per leg, or 1.4-3.0 W per 1 W resistor. Peak damper current 48 A x 4.99 R = 241 V per element. Cs 1.1 nF -> 184 uJ, 0.47 nF -> 188 uJ. V_DS peak 1379 V, the same as the deck's 1399 V. This loss is also missing from the efficiency table.
proposed_fix: Size the damper resistors for at least 7 W per leg with at least 300 V pulse rating, e.g. 2 x 4.99 R 10-20 W thick-film power resistors on the heatsink, or a series-parallel bank of pulse-rated 2512s. Replace the Coss-based estimate in calc() with the energy from a DPT deck that models the drawn RC at its real location, and add the damper loss to the loss budget.

location: 03_power; C301/C302 (leg A), C305/C306 (leg B) C4AQUBU4100A1WJ 1 uF; gen/pvcell.py calc() 'dec'
finding: The leg decoupling capacitors exceed their peak repetitive current rating at every hard turn-on. design_check splits only the 72.4 A load current between bank and decoupling, giving 26.9 A per capacitor against Ipkr 28 A. But the decoupling also supplies the Qoss of the two complementary devices plus the ringing, roughly doubling the peak.
evidence: docs/datasheets/passives-capacitors/C4AQ.pdf p14: C4AQUBU4100A1WJ Ipkr 28 A (dV/dt 28 V/us). p5: 1.5 x Ipkr is allowed only 1000 times per lifetime. Same ngspice model as PVR-02: decoupling-bank peak 115 A at 1100 V/72.4 A, 105 A at 950 V/62 A, 88 A at 800 V/45 A. That is 44-58 A per capacitor, or 44-58 V/us, at 32 kHz. The total loop current peaks at 141-185 A.
proposed_fix: Raise the pulse capability per leg: for example 4 x C4AQUBU4100A1WJ, or 2 x C4AQUBU4220A1YJ (2.2 uF, Ipkr 63 A, same p14 table). Verify it with a DPT deck that includes Qoss/Qrr, not with the inductive load-current split.

location: 05_sense; U501 AMC3302 (HGND/DCDC_HGND = L_A = SW_A through RS501); OC window U502/U503; gen/pvcell.py calc() 'isense'
finding: The inductor-current isolator, which feeds the local OC trip and AN1, has essentially no common-mode transient margin. Its HGND sits on the switch node SW_A, which slews 92 V/ns at turn-on (71 V/ns at turn-off). Its CMTI minimum is 95 V/ns. The design requires 1.5x CMTI margin for the gate drivers but asserts only 1.0x here. Disturbances longer than the 220 ns comparator filter will cause nuisance trips or corrupt the current signal.
evidence: docs/datasheets/sensing/AMC3302.pdf p8: CMTI 95 kV/us min, 155 typ, at |HGND-GND| = 2 kV. sim/out/pv_design/report.md sec 4: turn-on dv/dt 92 V/ns, so 95/92 = 1.03x. gen/pvcell.py line 290 asserts >= 1.5 x DVDT for UCC21710/UCC14241 but line 365 only asserts AMC3302 >= 1.0 x. In buck and band modes the shunt node switches every cycle.
proposed_fix: Either limit the switch-node dv/dt to 95/1.5 = 63 V/ns (higher Ron, and re-cost E_on), or measure the inductor current with a sensor rated for this dv/dt. Options are a busbar Hall/coreless sensor (ECO-09 allows it; LEM HO-NP / HLSR-P are already in docs/datasheets/sensing) or an isolated amplifier with CMTI >= 150 V/ns. Then apply the same 1.5x rule in calc().

location: 06_gd_a / 07_gd_b; NT601-NT604, NT701-NT704 (0 R net ties KS_Sxa/KS_Sxb to KS_Sx); Q301-Q308 pin 3
finding: The Kelvin sources of the two paralleled devices are joined at the driver star with 0 R. Together with the power-source busbar this closes a loop. Any source-inductance mismatch times di/dt drives a circulating current through the Kelvin bond wires and the gate-return traces, limited by no component. That current shifts each device's VGS during switching and can set off gate oscillation between the paralleled devices.
evidence: cell_spec worst_case_stresses turnoff_didt 5.6 A/ns per position = 2.8 A/ns per device. A 2 nH mismatch in source path gives 5.6 V around a loop of roughly 30 nH: about 2 A peak in roughly 10 ns, through pin 3 bond wires that have no current rating in docs/datasheets/power-semiconductors/MSC035SMA170B4.pdf (p2-3). The block note says 'power sources joined only by the busbar, never by the Kelvin traces', but the net ties join them at KS_Sx.
proposed_fix: Replace each Kelvin net tie with a pulse-rated 0.5-2.2 R (or a ferrite bead) per device, as in common paralleling practice. Keep each device's gate clamp and 10k on the device side of that resistor (see PVR-06).

finding: Each device's anti-series Zener clamp and 10k gate-source resistor return to the driver star KS_Sx, not to that device's own source-sense net KS_Sxa/KS_Sxb. The note asks for them 'at each device', but the netlist forces their source end to route back through the Kelvin trace and net tie. So the clamp limits gate-to-star voltage, not VGS at the die, and adds the Kelvin-loop inductance to the clamp loop.
evidence: Netlist KS_S1 = ... D604.3 D607.3 R614.2 R617.2 ... U603.3, while KS_S1a = NT601.1 Q301.3 only (likewise S2-S4). docs/datasheets/power-semiconductors/MSC035SMA170B4.pdf p2: VGS +23/-10 V static, +25/-12 V transient; clamp level +23.3 V at 5-10 mA (gdrv design_check). That leaves under 2 V for any Kelvin-loop drop.
proposed_fix: In gdrv.channel() connect the negative Zener and the 10k of gate i to the device's own Kelvin net (KS_Sxa / KS_Sxb). This means passing per-device source nets into channel() instead of the shared source.

location: 02_logic; U204 SN74LVC1G74 (/PRE=PRE_N, /CLR=EN_RX, /Q=FAULT_N); U205 gate 2 FLT_OK = DRV_FLT_N*RDY*FAULT_N
finding: A persisting local overcurrent or over-temperature fault is reported to the controller as healthy while EN is low. With /PRE and /CLR both low the 74LVC1G74 drives both Q and /Q high, so FAULT_N and FLT_OK go high even though PRE_N is still asserted. The controller cannot tell a cleared fault from a persisting one, for example heatsink OT, until it re-enables and the cell re-trips. Gating stays safe because the latch re-sets on EN rising.
evidence: docs/datasheets/isolation-interface/SN74LVC1G74.pdf p10 Table 8-1: PRE=L, CLR=L gives Q=H, /Q=H (nonstable). gen/pvcell.py lines 603-608.
proposed_fix: Report the live fault inputs as well: FLT_OK = DRV_FLT_N AND RDY AND FAULT_N AND PRE_N. For example, use a 4-input AND, or feed PRE_N into gate 2 and move FAULT_N via a spare gate.

location: 05_sense; RT501 (heatsink NTC, T_HS) with R513, U504A OT comparator; L401/J406 winding NTC (T_L) with R517
finding: An open heatsink-NTC lead (broken 200 mm probe lead or unplugged probe) disables the local 87 C OT trip without any indication. The NTC is the bottom element of the divider, so open means T_HS = REF2V5, which reads as the coldest temperature and keeps OT_OK high. AN2 cannot tell open from -40 C. The same applies to the winding NTC on AN3.
evidence: T_HS = 2.5 x R/(1k + R). Open gives 2.500 V. -40 C (R/R25 33.65, docs/datasheets/sensing/B57703M.pdf p4) gives 2.4926 V: a 7 mV difference, within OPA4322 VOS 2 mV plus the CTRL AFE error. The OT trip needs T_HS < TH_OT (1.25 V), so an open sensor never trips.
proposed_fix: For the heatsink NTC, swap the NTC and the 1k (REF2V5 - NTC - T_HS - 1k - AGND, threshold mirrored) so an open lead reads hot and trips. The heatsink is PE-bonded, so the noise argument for the winding NTC does not apply. Alternatively add an open-detect window (T_HS > 2.45 V means fault) to PRE_N. For the winding NTC, document a firmware plausibility check.

location: 05_sense; D501 LM4040AIM3-2.5 pin 3 (unconnected) - reference for the OC window, OT threshold and both NTC dividers
finding: Pin 3 of the 2.5 V shunt reference is left floating. The datasheet allows that only in quiet environments: with significant high-frequency switching noise, TI recommends tying pin 3 to the anode. This reference sets every local trip threshold, and it sits on a board with 92 V/ns switch nodes.
evidence: docs/datasheets/sensing/LM4040.pdf p4 Table 4-1 note 2: 'must be left floating or connected to pin 2 ... significant high-frequency switching noise, TI recommends to connect this pin to the anode'. Netlist: unconnected-(D501-NC-Pad3).
proposed_fix: Connect D501 pin 3 to AGND (the anode).
